items.rationale: Each model call is independent; the program re-sends the history. A larger window only raises how much can be sent, and the model has no memory of its own between calls.
Call 1 sends 1,000; call 2 sends 1,500; call 3 sends 2,000. Total 4,500. An answer of 2,000 gives only the final context size and misses that history is re-sent each call.

Persistence across sessions is the program's job: write the fact to storage and load it back. A bigger window or an open conversation does not survive a new session, and telling the model once keeps nothing.

items.answer: It costs fewer tokens on every call and avoids context rot, so the model finds the answer more accurately.
accepted: fewer tokens means lower cost and better accuracy
the whole manual costs tokens every call and degrades the model's recall

items.rationale: Every token in context is paid for on each call, and a long context reduces recall accuracy. Either reason, cost or accuracy, is a valid core; the best answers give both.

items.answer: Details left out of the summary are lost and cannot be recovered.
items.rationale: Compaction is lossy: exact values, such as a booking time, may not survive the summary. Keep exact values in notes or storage.
